**Perforeret hulorgan** (perforated hollow organ) is a severe, life-threatening acute surgical condition characterized by the rupture of a hollow viscus, which necessitates immediate medical intervention to prevent severe infection and sepsis. Within the Danish healthcare system's national quality improvement initiatives for acute surgery, it is recognized as a critical diagnosis where the timing of antibiotic therapy is exceptionally urgent to halt the progression of infection [^src1].

In the clinical guidelines outlined by the Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) draft from January 2026, medical professionals are strongly advised to initiate antibiotic treatment as rapidly as possible for patients suspected of suffering from a perforated hollow organ, severe ileus, or ischemia [^src1]. This recommendation applies universally to these suspected cases, regardless of whether the patient presents with a fever or shows altered infection markers in their blood work [^src1]. 

This condition is central to a broader systematic monitoring program led by the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut), which utilizes data from national registries like the Sygehusmedicinregisteret to track and improve acute surgical care [^src1]. Specifically, a perforated hollow organ defines a subgroup of patients for whom clinical quality indicators—such as the administration of antibiotics within three hours and CT scanning within two hours—are vital for ensuring early diagnosis and optimizing survival outcomes [^src1].

## Mentions
